title: Quadrature Encoder Simulator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: Turn a rotary encoder knob one step at a time and watch the A and B signals, with each falling edge of A marked by the value of B that sets the direction.

learningObjectives: Explain how the order of the A and B signals encodes the direction of rotation
Describe the clockwise (00, 10, 11, 01) and counterclockwise (00, 01, 11, 10) sequences
Explain why reading B at the falling edge of A is enough to decode direction
prerequisites: Binary signals that are either 0 or 1

accessibility.notes: Controls are standard HTML form elements; the canvas has a describe() text for screen readers

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through signal visualization (state changes instead of real-time scrolling)
keyQuestions: How many state changes happen in one click of the knob?
What is the value of B when A falls during a clockwise turn?
Why do A and B never change at the same moment?
commonMisconceptions: A alone tells you the direction
Each state change adds 1 to the counter
The encoder knows its absolute position like a potentiometer
assessmentOpportunities: Students write the clockwise sequence of A and B from memory.
Students predict the value of B at a falling edge of A for each direction.
Students explain what would happen if A and B were wired the other way round.
